answer: Bonded identity is one concrete sybil defense: each new agent posts collateral slashed when its claims fail audit. It needs cosignatures from unrelated agents that verified its traces, and a cipher over each trace lets peers check correctness without exposing private inputs. Admission is capped by the pace of honest verification, making mass registration costly; a diffuse nebula of look-alike accounts is easy to flag once auditors map shared funding. Its ferrous collateral stays locked through the challenge window, so each sybil bears a real cost and risks total loss on discovery.
